clusters.name: Your grandfather Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around the family's move across the country in March 1952, within the year: your grandmother June grew homesick and anxious, writing daily to her sister; your grandfather Walter distanced himself in the orchard; your father Glen began fights at school; your grandmother kept to her bed for weeks that first winter; your grandfather stopped speaking to his brother Harlan over their father's land money; your grandfather and grandmother fought over money for new trees. By September 1953, your grandmother joined the church choir and her letters thinned out, where the period settles.

clusters.name: Your grandfather Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968, when the late frost took the crop and the bank called in the loan: your grandfather Walter drank heavily; he and your father Glen blamed each other; your father took over the family's money and talks with the bank; your brother Carl's asthma attacks worsened; you began wetting the bed; your grandmother Ida's heart trouble was found. By October 1969, your grandfather stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, where the period settles.

clusters.name: Your father Glen losing his job at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around your father Glen losing his job in February 1975: he sat out in the truck for hours most of that year, out of work; he and your mother Marian fought loudly over money at night; your mother took a second job cleaning offices; you stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; you kept to your room and distanced from your mother; your grandfather Walter drank again after six years. By June 1976, you were eating again and made the track team, where the period settles.

clusters.name: Your mother-in-law Wilma moving into your house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move into your house in January 1990: you clashed with her over the children's bedtimes and meals; you and Hollis worked late and kept your distance; Hollis took his mother's side; your son Owen had tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over your daughter Lily's care; you and Hollis fought most nights; your eczema flared on both hands. By summer 1991, after Wilma took a flat in town in June, your eczema cleared.
